description.value: The Lions Bay General Store & Café is a long-standing Sea to Sky Corridor institution combining a liquor store — stocked with craft beer, wine, and ciders with an emphasis on Howe Sound and local producers — with a general store carrying artisan breads, fine meats, cheeses, and local souvenirs. The attached café serves coffee and a seasonal breakfast and lunch menu, and the 'Howe Sound Patio & Beer Garden' features live music on Saturdays. Situated in the small village of Lions Bay between Vancouver and Squamish, it is a natural resupply stop for cyclists on the Sea to Sky route.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record tags this node as 'Lions Bay Liquor' (shop=alcohol) at 350 Centre Road, Lions Bay, but the website at lionsbay.com identifies the broader business as 'The Lions Bay General Store & Café' — the liquor store is one component of a combined general store, café, and beer garden that has operated for over 30 years on the Sea to Sky Corridor. The website confirms the business is real and actively operating. No cycling-specific amenities (bike parking, washrooms, water refill) are mentioned anywhere on the website, so those remain null.
concerns: Name mismatch: OSM records this node as 'Lions Bay Liquor' but the website brands the entire establishment as 'The Lions Bay General Store & Café' — the liquor store is one department within a larger combined operation. The OSM record may benefit from a name correction or a note that this is part of the General Store.
No phone number is present in OSM or on the website content fetched.
Website address (lionsbay.com) was discovered rather than explicitly tagged in OSM; the site does correspond to this business.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, long-established, publicly accessible business on a popular cycling corridor; serves food, drink, and retail goods useful to touring cyclists passing through Lions Bay.

Takeout.detail: Café serves seasonal breakfast and lunch menu; general store sells packaged goods including beer, wine, spirits, meats, and cheeses — all inherently take-away
